chunks: And that which was narrated: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad from Aban from Hakim ibn Hukaym al-Sayrafi said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whichever slave is accompanied by his masters to perform Hajj, he has fulfilled the Hajj of Islam.'
It is to be understood as referring to the one whose master accompanied him to perform Hajj and freed him on the evening of Arafah or when he was standing at one of the two stations.
And that which indicates this is what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: When does a slave fulfill the obligatory Hajj if accompanied by his master?
ai.summary: In the Shia scholarly tradition, this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the condition of manumission timing relative to the Hajj rites, ensuring the slave's freedom is secured before the duty is considered complete. It highlights the juristic nuance that emancipation must occur during the pilgrimage period—specifically on the evening of Arafah or at the standing stations—to validate the 'Hajjat al-Islam' for the freed slave. This ruling underscores the interplay between social status (slavery) and religious obligation in early Islamic jurisprudence.
